text:
Alice: heads-up — customer 'orbital-pay' reports intermittent 504s from our Go SDK when they do aggressive client-side cancels + retries. Errors show up as 504 gateway_timeout in our logs, but the service returns 200 sometimes.
Ben: can you paste a minimal repro or their transport config? is this happening on dedicated or hosted?
Alice: hosted. Repro they gave: high qps (~300 rps), per-request ctx with 2s timeout, plus our SDK retry loop that retries idempotent requests up to 2 times. They also set a custom http.Client with a Transport that has DialContext and default IdleConnTimeout.
Carla: oh nice, we saw a similar-sounding case last quarter. common culprits: not attaching ctx to the Request, mixing client.Timeout with per-request ctx, or leaving resp.Body open which exhausts keepalive pool under high load. also transport config (MaxIdleConnsPerHost too low) can make retries wait/timeout.
Alice: here's the snippet they sent:
```go
tr := &http.Transport{
  DialContext: (&net.Dialer{Timeout: 30 * time.Second}).DialContext,
  MaxIdleConns: 10,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 2,
  IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second,
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr, Timeout: 2 * time.Second}

// in retry loop
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", url, body)
resp, err := client.Do(req.WithContext(ctx))
if err != nil {
  // retry logic
}
// they were not always deferring resp.Body.Close() in all branches
```
Ben: ok a few red flags: MaxIdleConnsPerHost=2 + high qps will exhaust the pool quickly; client.Timeout+ctx timeout can cause confusing behavior (client.Timeout is a hard deadline that cancels the whole request stack); and resp.Body not closed => connection leak.
Carla: recommended immediate mitigations we suggested to the customer:
- Ensure every code path calls resp.Body.Close() (even on non-2xx).
- Prefer per-request ctx instead of client.Timeout, i.e. remove client.Timeout if you already use req.WithContext(ctx).
- Increase MaxIdleConnsPerHost and MaxIdleConns. Example: 100/100 for 300 rps.
- As a temporary workaround, set Transport.DisableKeepAlives = true to avoid reusing potentially half-closed sockets (this hurts perf but stops the 504s).
Alice: I asked them to try the above and send us the net/http trace if still failing. they tried the fixes and saw 80% reduction in 504s. still occasional 504 under bursts.
Ben: next-level debug: enable httptrace to see whether cancellations happen during connection reuse or while writing the request body. Also check adapter-level retries in our SDK — older SDK versions retried after ctx cancel without re-attaching a fresh ctx to the secondary attempt. which SDK version are they on?
Alice: v1.3.0.
Ben: known issue — v1.3.0 had a bug where retry attempts reused the original request without re-binding a new ctx deadline for the subsequent attempt, causing the second attempt to immediately fail if the original ctx expired. patch landed in v1.3.4. ask them to upgrade to >=v1.3.4 or v1.4.x.
Carla: also show them a safer retry pattern we recommend: honor ctx for each attempt and compute a per-attempt timeout. e.g.:
```go
for i := 0; i < maxRetries; i++ {
  attemptCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctxParent, perAttempt)
  req = req.WithContext(attemptCtx)
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
  cancel()
  if err == nil {
    defer resp.Body.Close()
    // success
    break
  }
  // backoff, continue
}
```
Alice: I pushed a repro case into a sandbox and confirmed: with low MaxIdleConnsPerHost and missing Body.Close you see socket exhaustion and 504-like symptoms. with fixes applied, no more 504s under same load.
DeployBot: incident-note created: INC-2026-04 - go-sdk: retries+context race -> 504s (customer-impacting).
Carla: action items:
- [ ] Recommend customer upgrade to SDK v1.3.4+ (or v1.4.x)
- [ ] Provide sample client.Transport config and the safer retry snippet above
- [ ] Add a section in our docs about "Go SDK: best practices for context, timeouts, and transport" (include resp.Body.Close, per-request ctx, max idle connections guidance)
Alice: closing loop with customer; they'll test upgrade + transport tweaks and we asked for httptrace logs if issues persist. :thumbsup:
